programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see...a shape of one color surrounded by 4 single squares of another color.

The output grid size...will be the same size as the inside of the single 4 squares in the input grid.

To make the output, you have to...use the color of the single 4 boxes and replicate the shapes from the input grid.

content.text:
Let me understand the rule from the verifier.

Input: a shape of one color surrounded by 4 single squares of another color.

Verifier:
- x0 = asindices(I) - all indices
- x1 = corners(x0) - 4 corners of the grid
- x2 = mapply(dneighbors, x1) - neighbors of corners
- x3 = toobject(x2, I) - objects (color, index) at those neighbor positions
- x4 = mostcolor(x3) - most common color among those corner-neighbor cells (background color)
- x5 = palette(I) - all colors
- x6 = remove(x4, x5) - colors except background
- x7 = order(x6, identity) - sorted
- x8 = first(x7) - smaller color
- x9 = last(x7) - larger color
- x10 = ofcolor(I, x8) - indices of smaller color
- x11 = ofcolor(I, x9) - indices of larger color
- x12 = switch(I, x9, x8) - swap the two colors
- x13 = combine(x10, x11) - union of indices of both colors
- x14 = subgrid(x13, x12) - bounding box of the two colors in the swapped grid
- x15 = trim(x14) - remove border

So in the example: colors 4 and 9. x8=4, x9=9. Switch swaps 4<->9. Then subgrid over bounding box of all 4's and 9's. The 9's are the singles at corners positions (rows 8,17, cols 2,7). The 4 shape is inside. Bounding box from row 8 to 17, col 2 to 7. That's 10 rows x 6 cols. Wait output is 8x4.

Let's check: 4 cells occupy rows 9-15, cols 3-6. 9 cells at (8,2),(8,7),(17,2),(17,7). So bounding box rows 8-17 (10), cols 2-7 (6). trim removes border -> rows 9-16 (8), cols 3-6 (4). Output is 8x4. Yes.

After switch, 4->9 and 9->4. So the output shows the shape (originally 4) recolored to 9, and the 4 single squares become... wait the 9's at the border positions get trimmed away. Actually the border of the bounding box contains the 9's. After switch, those corner cells become 4, but they're on the border which gets trimmed.

So output = the inner shape (original color x8=4) recolored to x9=9, cropped to the region inside the 4 single squares. Essentially the inner shape region.

Wait, output shows the shape with color 9 (originally 4). And size = inner region (inside the 4 single boxes).

Let me verify output:

That's exactly the output with 4->9. Yes!

So rule: the output is the interior region (crop the bounding box of all non-background content and trim the border), with the shape color replaced by... the color of the 4 single squares.

Actually more precisely: x8 = smaller color, x9 = larger color (sorted). The shape is color x8, the 4 singles are color x9? In this example 4 is shape, 9 is singles. But x8=4 is "first" = smaller. Hmm but the singles could be the smaller color. Let's think: the output uses color x9 (the larger). And the shape gets recolored to x9.

Actually the rule says "use the color of the single 4 boxes and replicate the shapes". So output color = single boxes color. And in example the single boxes are 9. Yes.

But the verifier just sorts colors and uses first/last regardless of which is shape. Hmm. But if singles were smaller color, then x8=singles, x9=shape, and switch would swap so shape becomes smaller color... output color would be the smaller one. That contradicts the rule. But probably the generator always makes singles the larger color? Not necessarily.

Let me re-read: x8 = first = smaller color, x9 = last = larger. x10 = ofcolor(x8), x11 = ofcolor(x9). x12 = switch(I, x9, x8). x13 = combine(x10, x11). x14 = subgrid(x13, x12) - bounding box of both color sets. x15 = trim.

So the bounding box includes the singles. Then trim removes one layer. Since singles are at corners of the bounding box (aligned), trim removes them. Then output shows the shape, recolored by switch.

The switch swaps colors: shape originally color A becomes B, singles color B become A. After trim, singles gone. Output shape = B.

So the output color is always the color that is NOT the shape color, i.e., the singles color. Whether it's larger or smaller doesn't matter because switch handles it: shape becomes the other color. Right! switch swaps both. Shape A->B, singles B->A but trimmed. So output color = B = singles color. Good, works regardless of ordering.

So output: crop the interior (border removed) of the region containing the shape and singles, with all shape cells recolored to the singles color, background stays 0.

Essentially: output = shape pattern (in the inner region bounded by singles) with singles color.
